newsitem.title: USA: Northern plains power being restored after storm.
newsitem.headline: Northern plains power being restored after storm.

text.p: Electricity was being restored Tuesday in pockets of North Dakota and Minnesota that were hard hit by a weekend winter storm that cut power to over 50,000 electricity customers, utility officials said.

About 10,000 customers, primarily located in rural areas in North Dakota, remained without power as of early Tuesday, down from about 52,000 customers without power in Minnesota and North Dakota at the height of the storm on Sunday, the officials said.
Repair crews continued to battle mud and snow drifts up to 10 feet high to access damaged power facilities, said Lee Krogh, spokesman for Otter Tail Power Co.
"There will be people out of service for another two or three days," Krogh said.

Otter Tail had about 7,000 to 10,000 customers out of service in North Dakota and Minnesota as of Tuesday morning, down from about 25,000 customers out of service at the peak of the storm, the spokesman said.

Crews found severe damage as the storm abated Monday morning. In some cases, temporary repairs were necessary, and crews strung power lines around severely damaged transmission facilities, Krogh said.
"There are four of five high voltage transmission lines (estimated at about 345 kilovolts each) running east/west to North Dakota that have been knocked down," he said.
Otter Tail supplies power to about 124,000 customers through eastern North Dakota, western Minnesota and northeastern South Dakota.
"Overall, we are working to restore electricity to about 1,400 Northern States' customers (as of Tuesday morning)," said Mary Heimstead, spokeswoman for Northern States Power Co.
Northern States lost power to about 24,000 customers in North Dakota on Sunday.
Electricity should be fully restored to all Northern States customers by Wednesday, Heimstead said.
Northern States serves about 1.4 million customers in Minnesota, Wisconsin, North and South Dakota and Michigan.
The storm limited power transmission from Canada, Minnesota and North Dakota, Heimstead said.
"We are down to about eight towns without power, and they are all what you would call hamlets," said John Brookhart, spokesman for MDU Resources Group Inc subsidiary Montana-Dakota Utilities Co.
Less than 800 Montana-Dakota Utilities customers were without power as of early Tuesday, compared with about 3,000 without power at the height of the outages on Sunday, Brookhart said.
"Our line crews are having to fight some severe obstacles, like eight to 10 foot high snow drifts," he said.
Several large transmission lines were knocked out within the company's service territory, including a 230 kilovolt transmission line and two 115 kilovolt lines.
Montana-Dakota Utilities serves customers in western North Dakota, eastern Montana and northern South Dakota. The company is headquartered in Bismark, N.D.
